title: Gaussian integers
summary: $\mathbb Z[i]$ has unique factorization with norm $N(a+bi) = a^2 + b^2$. A prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ splits as $\pi\bar\pi$, $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ stays prime, and $2 = -i(1+i)^2$ ramifies.
why: The cleanest proof of the two-squares theorem, and the first number ring beyond $\mathbb Z$.
references: Ireland & Rosen, A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory

prerequisites.title: Primes and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic

title: Eisenstein integers
summary: $\mathbb Z[\omega]$ with $\omega = e^{2\pi i/3}$ is the ring of integers of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. It has unique factorization, six units, and norm $a^2 - ab + b^2$; primes $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ split.
why: The arena of cubic reciprocity, and of the 2026 quasi-RH manuscript.
references: Ireland & Rosen, A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory

prerequisites.title: Primes and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic

title: Ideals and rings of integers
summary: In a ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ elements may factor non-uniquely, but ideals factor uniquely into prime ideals (Dedekind, 1871). Kummer's ideal numbers (1847) were the precursor.
why: Ideal factorization is what number fields have instead of unique factorization.

timeline.title: Ideal numbers
timeline.text: Restored unique factorization in cyclotomic rings with ideal numbers and proved Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes.

timeline.title: Ideals
timeline.text: Defined ideals and proved unique factorization of ideals in rings of integers.

title: Class groups
summary: The ideal class group measures the failure of unique factorization; its order is the class number $h_K$. Imaginary quadratic fields with $h = 1$ are exactly $d = 1,2,3,7,11,19,43,67,163$.
why: Class numbers of imaginary quadratic fields grow, but how fast is tied to Siegel zeros.
references: Cox, Primes of the Form x² + ny²

title: Cyclotomic fields
summary: $\mathbb Q(\zeta_n)$ has degree $\varphi(n)$, and $p \nmid n$ splits into $\varphi(n)/f$ primes, where $f$ is the order of $p$ modulo $n$. Gauss used $\mathbb Q(\zeta_{17})$ in 1796 to construct the regular 17-gon.
key_statements: \Phi_n(x) = \prod_{\substack{1 \le k \le n \\ \gcd(k,n)=1}} \bigl(x - e^{2\pi i k/n}\bigr), \qquad [\mathbb Q(\zeta_n):\mathbb Q] = \varphi(n)
why: By Kronecker–Weber every abelian extension of $\mathbb Q$ lies in a cyclotomic field.
references: Ireland & Rosen, A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory

timeline.title: The regular 17-gon
timeline.text: Constructed it with ruler and compass using $\mathbb Q(\zeta_{17})$.

timeline.title: Ideal numbers
timeline.text: Restored unique factorization in cyclotomic rings with ideal numbers and proved Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes.

title: Cubic characters and cubic reciprocity
summary: For $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ there are two characters of order $3$ modulo $p$. Eisenstein proved cubic reciprocity in $\mathbb Z[\omega]$ in 1844; cubic Gauss sums satisfy $g(\chi)^3 = p\,J(\chi,\chi)$ with a Jacobi sum $J$.
why: Cubic theta sums built from these characters drive the 2026 quasi-RH manuscript.
references: Ireland & Rosen, A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory

timeline.title: Quasi-RH manuscript (7/8)
timeline.text: Claims every Dirichlet $L$-function is zero-free in $\operatorname{Re}s > \tfrac78$, using Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$, cubic theta sums and a Mellin continuation. Reported as Lean-verified.

timeline.title: Improving the 7/8 half-plane
timeline.text: Varies the parameters of the cubic theta argument to widen the zero-free half-plane.

title: Dedekind zeta functions
summary: $\zeta_K(s) = \sum_{\mathfrak a} N\mathfrak a^{-s}$ over nonzero ideals of $\mathcal O_K$. For a quadratic field it factors as $\zeta(s)L(s,\chi_D)$, and its residue at $s=1$ carries the class number.
why: The factorization moves questions about a number field down to $\mathbb Q$.

timeline.title: Ideals
timeline.text: Defined ideals and proved unique factorization of ideals in rings of integers.
